newsitem.title: UK: New Hanson H1 pretax profit 262.8 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: New Hanson H1 pretax profit 262.8 mln stg.

text.p: The new Hanson Plc, a rump building materials group left over from the company's four-way split demerger, reported first-half pretax profits of 262.8 million pounds ($431.7 million) on Thursday which included a five month contribution from the former Energy Group division.

The continued operations operating profit for Hanson's remaining building businesses was 69.6 million pounds in the year ended March 31, compared to 66.3 million the previous year. Analysts said this gave a more accurate picture of the group's progress. No dividend was paid in the first half.
The group also took the chance to announce that chairman Lord Hanson will step down at the end of 1997, to be succeeded by Chistopher Collins, the current deputy chairman.
Lord Hanson, founder of the once-mighty conglomerate, said the outlook for the rump group was bright.

"The signs of improvement in the UK housing and construction markets are now more evident, the prospects for our U.S. businesses are good and we look forward to making steady progress during the rest of 1997."
He said the division spanning building materials and construction had made "solid progress" in the first half.

The net debt of the group was 325 million, up from 174 million. This excludes the 125 million cash spoils received in April from the sale of Hanson Electrical and the 78 million cost of buying Concrete Pipe & Products.
